standfirst: Underneath the neighbourhood comedy this was a burnout story: a woman who quit everything and came home without being able to say why. The right recommendations understand that the mothers, the hometown and the slow recovery were the show, and the romance was the frame around it.

picks.why: Two people with a shared childhood and a specific history of hurting each other, forced back into the same frame and having to be honest about it. Same texture of ordinary conversations doing the heavy lifting. Difference: the families are almost absent, so all the weight lands on the couple rather than the street they grew up on.

The comfort standard: a woman leaves a career that was eating her, lands in a town that will not leave her alone, and slowly stops performing competence. The ensemble is the point in both shows. Difference: it is warmer and lighter throughout, with none of the family shouting matches that give your show its edges.

Burnout, a hometown, a mother, and a sibling relationship that carries more than the romance does. The scenes about not being able to admit you have broken down are the best written in either series. Difference: the swapped-lives premise adds a mechanism your show did not need, and the tone is sadder for longer.

A small town, a woman the neighbourhood has opinions about, and a green flag lead who simply keeps showing up. The comedy and the ache sit in the same scene, which is the trick your show pulls in its better hours. Difference: there is a serial killer subplot running through it, so the register is much wider.

Quitting the job and the city, then doing nothing on purpose. It is the quietest possible version of the choice your heroine makes in episode one, and it does not rush her recovery. Difference: almost no plot, no family pressure and a very slow pulse, so it asks for patience rather than momentum.

An ensemble about ordinary people in a coastal town, told one chapter at a time, where the parent and child stories hit harder than the couples. Same faith that small lives are enough material. Difference: it is an anthology with no central romance, so nothing carries across the whole run.

against.title: Welcome to Samdal-ri
against.why: The obvious pairing: hometown return, childhood friend, ensemble of neighbours. It is the same shape with a thinner script, and it never finds a real subject underneath the comedy the way your show finds burnout.

against.title: Something in the Rain
against.why: Recommended because of Jung Hae In. It is an age-gap office romance with a very different anxiety at its centre, and its family scenes exist to punish the couple rather than to explain them.

against.title: Start-Up
against.why: Paired for the ambitious young professional angle. It is a glossy career drama about winning, where your show is about the aftermath of losing, and the two have almost nothing in common emotionally.
